   915→// BuildTreeFromEntries builds a proper git tree structure from flattened file entries.
   916→// Exported for use by strategy package (push_common.go, session_test.go)
   917→func BuildTreeFromEntries(repo *git.Repository, entries map[string]object.TreeEntry) (plumbing.Hash, error) {
   918→	// Build a tree structure
   919→	root := &treeNode{
   920→		entries: make(map[string]*treeNode),
   921→		files:   []object.TreeEntry{},
   922→	}
   923→
   924→	// Insert all entries into the tree structure
   925→	for fullPath, entry := range entries {
   926→		parts := strings.Split(fullPath, "/")

   934→// insertIntoTree inserts a file entry into the tree structure.
   935→func insertIntoTree(node *treeNode, pathParts []string, entry object.TreeEntry) {

   937→		// This is a file in the current directory
   938→		node.files = append(node.files, object.TreeEntry{
   939→			Name: pathParts[0],
   940→			Mode: entry.Mode,
   941→			Hash: entry.Hash,
   942→		})
   943→		return
   944→	}
   945→
   946→	// This is in a subdirectory
   947→	dirName := pathParts[0]

   950→			entries: make(map[string]*treeNode),
   951→			files:   []object.TreeEntry{},
   952→		}
   953→	}
   954→	insertIntoTree(node.entries[dirName], pathParts[1:], entry)

   957→// buildTreeObject recursively builds tree objects from a treeNode.
   958→func buildTreeObject(repo *git.Repository, node *treeNode) (plumbing.Hash, error) {
   959→	var treeEntries []object.TreeEntry
   960→
   961→	// Add files
   962→	treeEntries = append(treeEntries, node.files...)
   963→
   964→	// Recursively build subtrees
   965→	for name, subnode := range node.entries {
   966→		subHash, err := buildTreeObject(repo, subnode)
   967→		if err != nil {
   968→			return plumbing.ZeroHash, err
   969→		}
   970→		treeEntries = append(treeEntries, object.TreeEntry{
   971→			Name: name,
   972→			Mode: filemode.Dir,
   973→			Hash: subHash,
   974→		})
   975→	}
   976→
   977→	// Sort entries (git requires sorted entries)
   978→	sortTreeEntries(treeEntries)
   979→
   980→	// Create tree object
   981→	tree := &object.Tree{Entries: treeEntries}
   982→
   983→	obj := repo.Storer.NewEncodedObject()
   984→	if err := tree.Encode(obj); err != nil {
   985→		return plumbing.ZeroHash, fmt.Errorf("failed to encode tree: %w", err)
   986→	}
   987→
   988→	hash, err := repo.Storer.SetEncodedObject(obj)
   989→	if err != nil {
   990→		return plumbing.ZeroHash, fmt.Errorf("failed to store tree: %w", err)
   991→	}

   993→	return hash, nil

   996→// sortTreeEntries sorts tree entries in git's required order.
   997→// Git sorts tree entries by name, with directories having a trailing /
   998→func sortTreeEntries(entries []object.TreeEntry) {
   999→	sort.Slice(entries, func(i, j int) bool {
  1000→		nameI := entries[i].Name
  1001→		nameJ := entries[j].Name
  1002→		if entries[i].Mode == filemode.Dir {
  1003→			nameI += "/"
  1004→		}
  1005→		if entries[j].Mode == filemode.Dir {
  1006→			nameJ += "/"
  1007→		}
  1008→		return nameI < nameJ
  1009→	})
  1010→}

  1012→// collectChangedFiles collects all changed files (modified tracked + untracked non-ignored)
  1013→// using git CLI. This is much faster than filesystem walk and respects all gitignore sources
  1014→// including global gitignore (core.excludesfile).
  1015→//
  1016→// Uses git CLI instead of go-git because go-git's worktree.Status() does not respect
  1017→// global gitignore, which can cause globally ignored files to appear as untracked.
  1018→// See: https://github.com/entireio/cli/pull/129
  1019→//
  1020→// changedFilesResult contains both changed and deleted files from git status.
  1021→type changedFilesResult struct {
  1022→	Changed []string // Files to include (modified, added, untracked, renamed, etc.)
  1023→	Deleted []string // Files that were deleted (need to be excluded from checkpoint tree)
  1024→}
  1025→
  1026→// collectChangedFiles returns all changed files from git status for the first checkpoint.
  1027→//
  1028→// For the first checkpoint, we need to capture:
  1029→// - Modified tracked files (user's uncommitted changes)
  1030→// - Untracked non-ignored files (new files not yet added to git)
  1031→// - Renamed/copied files (both source removal and destination)
  1032→// - Deleted files (to exclude from checkpoint tree)
  1033→//
  1034→// The base tree from HEAD already contains all unchanged tracked files.
  1035→//
  1036→// Uses `git status --porcelain -z` for reliable parsing of filenames with special characters.
  1037→func collectChangedFiles(ctx context.Context, repo *git.Repository) (changedFilesResult, error) {
  1038→	// Get repo root directory for running git command
  1039→	wt, err := repo.Worktree()
  1040→	if err != nil {
  1041→		return changedFilesResult{}, fmt.Errorf("failed to get worktree: %w", err)
  1042→	}
  1043→	repoRoot := wt.Filesystem.Root()
  1044→
  1045→	// Use -z for NUL-separated output (handles quoted filenames with spaces/special chars)
  1046→	// Use -uall to list individual untracked files instead of collapsed directories.
  1047→	// Note: CLAUDE.md warns against -uall for user-facing display, but we need the full list
  1048→	// for checkpointing.
  1049→	cmd := exec.CommandContext(ctx, "git", "status", "--porcelain", "-z", "-uall")
  1050→	cmd.Dir = repoRoot
  1051→	output, err := cmd.Output()
  1052→	if err != nil {
  1053→		return changedFilesResult{}, fmt.Errorf("failed to get git status in %s: %w", repoRoot, err)
  1054→	}
  1055→
  1056→	changedSeen := make(map[string]struct{})
  1057→	deletedSeen := make(map[string]struct{})
  1058→
  1059→	// Parse NUL-separated output
  1060→	// Format: XY filename\0 (for most entries)
  1061→	// For renames/copies: XY newname\0oldname\0
  1062→	entries := strings.Split(string(output), "\x00")
  1063→
  1064→	for i := 0; i < len(entries); i++ {
  1065→		entry := entries[i]
  1066→		if len(entry) < 3 {
  1067→			continue
  1068→		}
  1069→
  1070→		// git status --porcelain format: XY filename
  1071→		// X = staging status, Y = worktree status
  1072→		staging := entry[0]
  1073→		wtStatus := entry[1]
  1074→		filename := entry[3:] // No TrimSpace needed with -z format
  1075→
  1076→		// Handle R/C (rename/copy) first - they have a second entry we must skip
  1077→		// even if the new filename is an infrastructure path
  1078→		if staging == 'R' || staging == 'C' {
  1079→			// Renamed or copied: current entry is new name, next entry is old name
  1080→			if !paths.IsInfrastructurePath(filename) {
  1081→				changedSeen[filename] = struct{}{}
  1082→			}
  1083→			// The old name follows as the next NUL-separated entry - must always skip it
  1084→			if i+1 < len(entries) && entries[i+1] != "" {
  1085→				oldName := entries[i+1]
  1086→				if staging == 'R' && !paths.IsInfrastructurePath(oldName) {
  1087→					// For renames, old file is effectively deleted
  1088→					deletedSeen[oldName] = struct{}{}
  1089→				}
  1090→				i++ // Skip the old name entry
  1091→			}
  1092→			continue
  1093→		}
  1094→
  1095→		// Skip .entire directory for non-R/C entries
  1096→		if paths.IsInfrastructurePath(filename) {
  1097→			continue
  1098→		}
  1099→
  1100→		// Handle different status codes
  1101→		switch {
  1102→		case staging == 'D' || wtStatus == 'D':
  1103→			// Deleted file - track separately
  1104→			deletedSeen[filename] = struct{}{}
  1105→
  1106→		case wtStatus == 'M' || wtStatus == 'A':
  1107→			// Modified or added in worktree
  1108→			changedSeen[filename] = struct{}{}
  1109→
  1110→		case staging == '?' && wtStatus == '?':
  1111→			// Untracked file
  1112→			changedSeen[filename] = struct{}{}
  1113→
  1114→		case staging == 'A' || staging == 'M':
  1115→			// Staged add or modify
  1116→			changedSeen[filename] = struct{}{}
  1117→
  1118→		case staging == 'T' || wtStatus == 'T':
  1119→			// Type change (e.g., file to symlink)
  1120→			changedSeen[filename] = struct{}{}
  1121→
  1122→		case staging == 'U' || wtStatus == 'U':
  1123→			// Unmerged (conflict) - include current file state
  1124→			changedSeen[filename] = struct{}{}
  1125→		}
  1126→	}
  1127→
  1128→	changed := make([]string, 0, len(changedSeen))
  1129→	for file := range changedSeen {
  1130→		changed = append(changed, file)
  1131→	}
  1132→
  1133→	deleted := make([]string, 0, len(deletedSeen))
  1134→	for file := range deletedSeen {
  1135→		deleted = append(deleted, file)
  1136→	}
  1137→
  1138→	return changedFilesResult{Changed: changed, Deleted: deleted}, nil
  1139→}

Here's how it works:

`getCondensedFilesTouched` reads `summary.FilesTouched` from the checkpoint metadata on `entire/checkpoints/v1`. This is the list of files the **agent** touched during the session — it was saved as `state.FilesTouched` during condensation.

The differentiation comes from the **overlap check** on line 345:

```go
if len(filesToCheck) == 0 || hasOverlappingFiles(stagedFiles, filesToCheck)
```

**Scenario: agent touched A, B, C → user commits A, B → user edits D → user commits D**

1. First commit: condensation runs, metadata records `files_touched: [A, B, C]`, `LastCheckpointID` is set.

2. Second commit (just D): PrepareCommitMsg fires. `FilesTouched` is nil, `StepCount == 0`, so it falls back to `getCondensedFilesTouched` which returns `[A, B, C]`. Then `hasOverlappingFiles(stagedFiles=["D"], filesToCheck=["A","B","C"])` returns **false** — D is not in the agent's file list. So `checkpointID` stays empty → **no trailer is added**. The commit is correctly treated as unrelated to the session.

**Scenario: agent touched A, B, C → user commits A, B → user commits C**

Same flow, but `hasOverlappingFiles(["C"], ["A","B","C"])` returns **true** → the trailer IS added, reusing `LastCheckpointID`. This correctly links the split commit.

**Edge case: user manually edits A (same file the agent touched) → commits A**

`hasOverlappingFiles(["A"], ["A","B","C"])` returns **true** → trailer added. This is a **false positive** — the user's manual edit gets linked to the agent session. The system can't distinguish "user edited file A independently" from "user is committing the agent's changes to A in a second commit." It errs on the side of linking, which is the safer default (preserves session context).

So: the differentiation is purely **file-name overlap**, not content-based. It can't tell if the user independently modified a file the agent also touched.

OK, here's the full picture. Two scenarios after carry-forward:

**Scenario A: User commits the remaining file C before a new prompt**

1. Carry-forward left: `state.Phase = ACTIVE`, `FilesTouched = ["C"]`, `StepCount = 1`, `LastCheckpointID = <cpID from first commit>`, shadow branch at new HEAD with C + metadata.

2. PrepareCommitMsg fires. `sessionHasNewContent` checks shadow branch — transcript has same number of lines as `CheckpointTranscriptStart` → no new content. Falls to `LastCheckpointID` reuse path. `FilesTouched = ["C"]`, staged files include "C" → overlap → **reuses same checkpoint ID**. Trailer added.

3. PostCommit fires. `hasNew = false`. `ActionCondense` but `hasNew` is false → **skips condensation**, just updates BaseCommit. `condensed = false` → carry-forward block skipped.

Result: Second commit gets the **same** checkpoint ID as the first. No new condensation. The metadata from the first condensation (which recorded `files_touched: [A, B, C]`) already covers file C. This is the existing split-commit behavior — works correctly.

**Scenario B: New prompt runs while C is still uncommitted**

1. `InitializeSession` called (UserPromptSubmit). Session already exists at current HEAD.

2. Line 1189: **`LastCheckpointID` is cleared** (fresh prompt = fresh checkpoint linkage).

3. `migrateShadowBranchIfNeeded` — HEAD hasn't moved (no commit since carry-forward), so shadow branch stays put. The carry-forward shadow branch at the current HEAD **survives**.

4. Agent works, touches file D. `SaveChanges` calls `store.WriteTemporary` with `BaseCommit = state.BaseCommit` (current HEAD). `getOrCreateShadowBranch` finds the existing carry-forward shadow branch → **appends** a new commit on top of it. Shadow branch now has C + D + updated metadata.

5. `state.FilesTouched` accumulates: `["C", "D"]`, `StepCount = 2`.

6. User commits C, D → condensation runs normally, carry-forward finds no remaining files → clean state.

Result: The carry-forward shadow branch seamlessly becomes the base for the next prompt's checkpoints. The agent's new work is layered on top of the carried-forward files. Works correctly.

**The one subtlety**: In Scenario B, the attribution calculation at line 1198 will see file C as a "user edit" (it was in the worktree before the prompt started but isn't in the base commit tree). That's arguably correct — the agent wrote it in a previous turn, but since the user chose not to commit it, it's part of the pre-prompt state.

Here's the full summary of the carry-forward feature and the open design question.

---

## Problem

When an agent makes multiple commits within a single turn (e.g., commits 2 of 3 edited files, then commits the third), the second commit gets no checkpoint. After the first commit's condensation, `StepCount` resets to 0, `FilesTouched` is cleared, and the shadow branch is deleted. The second commit sees no session data to condense.

## What's Implemented (in working tree now)

**Files changed:** `manual_commit_hooks.go`, `phase_postcommit_test.go`

**Core logic in PostCommit:**
1. Compute `committedFileSet` from the HEAD commit (diff vs parent)
2. Save `filesTouchedBefore` before the action dispatch loop (condensation clears it)
3. After condensation succeeds for an ACTIVE session, compute `remaining = filesTouchedBefore - committedFileSet`
4. If remaining files exist, call `carryForwardToNewShadowBranch`

**`carryForwardToNewShadowBranch`** creates a new shadow branch at the new HEAD (via `store.WriteTemporary`) containing the remaining files + metadata. Updates state: `FilesTouched = remaining`, `StepCount = 1`.

**Helper functions:**
- `filesChangedInCommit(commit)` — diffs commit vs parent, returns file set
- `subtractFiles(files, exclude)` — set subtraction

**The old shadow branch** (at old HEAD) is still deleted normally — the new one is at the new HEAD, so it's a different branch name and isn't in `shadowBranchesToDelete`.

## The Open Question: How to Signal "Needs Condensation"

After carry-forward, the next commit needs to:
1. **PrepareCommitMsg**: Generate a fresh checkpoint ID (not reuse old one)
2. **PostCommit**: Trigger condensation (not skip it)

Both rely on `sessionHasNewContent`, which checks `transcriptLines > CheckpointTranscriptStart`. After carry-forward the transcript hasn't grown → returns false → no trailer, no condensation.

### Approach A: Reset `CheckpointTranscriptStart = 0` (currently in code)

**How:** In `carryForwardToNewShadowBranch`, set `state.CheckpointTranscriptStart = 0`.

**Pros:**
- Simple, no new fields
- Works end-to-end — `sessionHasNewContent` returns true, PrepareCommitMsg generates fresh ID, PostCommit condenses

**Cons:**
- **Token usage is inflated** — condensation counts tokens from line 0, re-counting the entire transcript
- **Summary covers entire transcript** — `transcript.SliceFromLine(transcript, 0)` returns everything, so the summary is for the full session not just the delta
- **Stored metadata lies** — `checkpoint_transcript_start: 0` in the condensed metadata implies this was a first condensation
- Semantically overloads the transcript cursor for a different purpose

### Approach B: `HasCarryForward` boolean on SessionState

**How:** Add `HasCarryForward bool` to `SessionState`. Set in `carryForwardToNewShadowBranch`, check at the top of `sessionHasNewContent` (return true immediately), clear in `condenseAndUpdateState`.

**Pros:**
- `CheckpointTranscriptStart` stays correct — token counting and summary scoping work accurately for the carry-forward checkpoint
- Explicit, self-documenting signal — no ambiguity about why condensation triggers
- Easy to clear (condensation already resets session state fields)

**Cons:**
- New persistent field on SessionState (serialized to JSON in `.git/entire-sessions/`)
- One more thing to maintain/test
- Slightly more code

### Approach C: Use existing field combination as signal

# Carry Forward: Preserve Uncommitted Files After Condensation

## Problem

When an agent makes multiple commits within a single turn (e.g., commits 2 of 3 edited files, then commits the third), the second commit gets no checkpoint. After the first commit's condensation, `StepCount` resets to 0, `FilesTouched` is cleared, and the shadow branch is deleted. The second commit sees no session data to condense.

**Goal:** Every commit gets its own checkpoint with its own unique checkpoint ID. No checkpoint should be shared across two commits — duplicate data on the checkpoints branch is acceptable.

## What's Implemented (in working tree)

**Files changed:** `manual_commit_hooks.go`, `phase_postcommit_test.go`

### Core Logic in PostCommit

1. Compute `committedFileSet` from the HEAD commit (diff commit vs parent tree)
2. Save `filesTouchedBefore` before the action dispatch loop (condensation clears `FilesTouched`)
3. After condensation succeeds for an ACTIVE session, compute `remaining = filesTouchedBefore - committedFileSet`
4. If remaining files exist, call `carryForwardToNewShadowBranch`

### `carryForwardToNewShadowBranch`

Creates a new shadow branch at the new HEAD (via `store.WriteTemporary`) containing the remaining files + metadata directory. Updates state:

- `FilesTouched = remaining`
- `StepCount = 1`
- `LastCheckpointID = ""` (cleared — next commit must generate a fresh ID)

The old shadow branch (at old HEAD) is deleted normally. The new one is at the new HEAD (different branch name), so it survives cleanup.

### Helper Functions

- `filesChangedInCommit(commit)` — diffs commit against parent tree, returns `map[string]struct{}` of changed file paths
- `subtractFiles(files, exclude)` — returns files not in the exclude set

## Open Question: Content Detection Signal

After carry-forward, the next commit needs to:

1. **PrepareCommitMsg**: Generate a fresh checkpoint ID (not reuse the old one)
2. **PostCommit**: Trigger condensation (not skip it)

Both rely on `sessionHasNewContent()`, which checks `transcriptLines > CheckpointTranscriptStart`. After carry-forward the transcript hasn't grown, so it returns false — no trailer added, no condensation triggered.

We need a signal that says "this session has carry-forward content that needs its own checkpoint."

---

### Approach A: Reset `CheckpointTranscriptStart = 0`

**Currently in the code.**

In `carryForwardToNewShadowBranch`, set `state.CheckpointTranscriptStart = 0`.

This makes `sessionHasNewContent` see the shadow branch transcript (N lines) as all new (`N > 0` is true), triggering both trailer generation and condensation.

**Pros:**

- Simple — no new fields, no structural changes
- Works end-to-end for both PrepareCommitMsg and PostCommit

**Cons:**

- **Token usage inflated**: Condensation counts tokens from line 0, re-counting the entire transcript. The carry-forward checkpoint's token usage will include tokens from before the first commit.
- **Summary covers full transcript**: `transcript.SliceFromLine(transcript, 0)` returns everything. The summary generator processes the entire session history, not just the work since the last condensation.
- **Stored metadata is misleading**: `checkpoint_transcript_start: 0` in the condensed metadata implies this was a first condensation, when it's actually a continuation.
- **Semantically overloads** the transcript cursor for a purpose it wasn't designed for.

---

### Approach B: `HasCarryForward` Boolean on SessionState

Add `HasCarryForward bool` field to `SessionState` (persisted in `.git/entire-sessions/<session>.json`).

- **Set** in `carryForwardToNewShadowBranch`: `state.HasCarryForward = true`
- **Checked** at the top of `sessionHasNewContent`: if true, return true immediately
- **Cleared** in `condenseAndUpdateState`: `state.HasCarryForward = false`

**Pros:**

- `CheckpointTranscriptStart` stays at its real value — token counting and summary scoping are correct for the carry-forward checkpoint (only the delta gets processed)
- Explicit, self-documenting signal — no ambiguity about why condensation triggers
- Easy to reason about: carry-forward sets flag, condensation clears it

**Cons:**

- New persistent field on `SessionState` (serialized to JSON)
- One more field to maintain, test, and document
- Slightly more code (field definition, set/check/clear in three places)

---

### Approach C: Infer from Existing Field Combination

In `sessionHasNewContent`, after the transcript-based check returns false, add a fallback:

```go
if state.StepCount > 0 && len(state.FilesTouched) > 0 {
    return true, nil
}
```

**Reasoning:** After condensation, `StepCount = 0` and `FilesTouched = nil`. Carry-forward sets `StepCount = 1` and `FilesTouched = [remaining]`. This combination only exists after carry-forward.

**Pros:**

- No new fields on SessionState
- `CheckpointTranscriptStart` stays correct
- Minimal code change

**Cons:**

- **Implicitly coupled**: A normal session after `SaveChanges` (before any condensation) also has `StepCount > 0` and `FilesTouched` non-empty. The transcript check would already return true in that case, so the fallback is redundant — but this reasoning is fragile. A future change could break the assumption.
- Less self-documenting — the "why" isn't obvious without comments explaining the carry-forward context.
- Testing the signal requires understanding the invariant (condensation resets both fields, carry-forward sets both).

---

### Comparison

| Aspect | A: Reset cursor | B: Boolean flag | C: Infer from fields |
|---|---|---|---|
| New fields | None | `HasCarryForward` | None |
| Token accuracy | Inflated (full transcript) | Correct (delta only) | Correct (delta only) |
| Summary accuracy | Full transcript | Delta only | Delta only |
| Metadata accuracy | Misleading (`start: 0`) | Correct | Correct |
| Explicitness | Implicit (cursor abuse) | Explicit | Implicit (field combo) |
| Fragility | Low | Low | Medium |
| Code complexity | Minimal | Low | Minimal |

## Separate Concern: IDLE Split-Commit Behavior

The carry-forward guard is `condensed && state.Phase.IsActive()`, so IDLE sessions are unaffected.

Current IDLE split-commit behavior: when the user manually splits agent work across multiple commits, PrepareCommitMsg **reuses the same `LastCheckpointID`** via the `getCondensedFilesTouched` fallback. Both commits share a checkpoint ID.

This contradicts the "each commit gets its own checkpoint" principle but is pre-existing behavior, not introduced by carry-forward. Fixing it is a separate task.

## Tests

Two tests in `phase_postcommit_test.go`:

- **`TestPostCommit_ActiveSession_CarriesForwardRemainingFiles`**: 3 files touched, 2 committed → remaining file carried forward, `StepCount=1`, `FilesTouched=["C.txt"]`, new shadow branch exists at new HEAD.
- **`TestPostCommit_ActiveSession_NoCarryForward_WhenAllFilesCommitted`**: 2 files touched, 2 committed → no carry-forward, `StepCount=0`, `FilesTouched=nil`, old shadow branch deleted.

Tests will need updating based on which approach is chosen (A checks `CheckpointTranscriptStart=0`, B would check `HasCarryForward=true`, C would check neither).

## How it works today (at HEAD)

### State machine phases

There are **4 phases**: `IDLE`, `ACTIVE`, `ACTIVE_COMMITTED`, `ENDED`

### The two commit scenarios

**Scenario 1: IDLE commit (user commits between turns)**
```
IDLE + GitCommit → IDLE + ActionCondense
```
- Condense immediately in PostCommit
- `LastCheckpointID` is set from the commit trailer
- Shadow branch is deleted
- **On next commit**: PrepareCommitMsg checks if staged files overlap with `LastCheckpointID`'s files → **reuses the same checkpoint ID**

**Scenario 2: ACTIVE commit (agent commits mid-turn)**
```
ACTIVE + GitCommit → ACTIVE_COMMITTED + ActionMigrateShadowBranch
```
- **Does NOT condense** — just migrates the shadow branch to the new HEAD
- Stores `PendingCheckpointID` from the commit trailer
- If another commit happens: `ACTIVE_COMMITTED + GitCommit → ACTIVE_COMMITTED + ActionMigrateShadowBranch` (migrates again, same PendingCheckpointID)
- When agent finishes: `ACTIVE_COMMITTED + TurnEnd → IDLE + ActionCondense` — **deferred condensation** using PendingCheckpointID

### The "shared checkpoint" problem

Both scenarios lead to **multiple commits sharing one checkpoint ID**:

1. **ACTIVE multi-commit**: Agent makes commits A, B, C during one turn. All get the same `PendingCheckpointID` in PrepareCommitMsg. Condensation happens once at TurnEnd. Result: 3 commits, 1 checkpoint.

2. **IDLE split-commit**: User splits agent work across commits. First commit condenses. Second commit reuses `LastCheckpointID` via file overlap check. Result: 2 commits, 1 checkpoint.

### Why this exists: token counting

The key benefit of the current approach is **accurate token counting**. Condensation happens once per turn, counting the transcript delta (`CheckpointTranscriptStart` → current transcript length). The tokens counted match exactly the work done in the turn.

If you condense at every commit mid-turn, you'd need to decide: what transcript lines belong to commit 1 vs commit 2? The transcript is a continuous stream — the agent doesn't delineate "now I'm working on commit 1, now commit 2."

### The problems with shared checkpoints

1. **Conceptual mismatch**: A checkpoint should map 1:1 to a commit. Looking at `git log`, each commit has `Entire-Checkpoint: abc123`, but they all point to the same metadata on `entire/checkpoints/v1`. This is confusing for users and tools.

2. **Rewind ambiguity**: If 3 commits share checkpoint `abc123`, and you want to rewind to "after commit 2", the checkpoint doesn't distinguish states.

3. **Attribution difficulty**: Which commit contributed what? The checkpoint has aggregate data, not per-commit data.

---

## The alternative: one checkpoint per commit always

Your carry-forward branch changes the approach:

```
ACTIVE + GitCommit → ACTIVE + ActionCondense (immediate)
```

- No `ACTIVE_COMMITTED` phase
- No `PendingCheckpointID`
- No deferred condensation
- No shadow branch migration

After condensation, if remaining uncommitted files exist, `carryForwardToNewShadowBranch` creates a new shadow branch at the new HEAD.

### What this solves
- Every commit gets exactly one checkpoint ID
- Clean 1:1 mapping between commits and checkpoints
- No shared checkpoint confusion

### The open problem: token counting after carry-forward

After condensation clears `CheckpointTranscriptStart` and carry-forward creates a new shadow branch, the next commit needs to trigger condensation again. But the transcript hasn't grown (the agent's still working). `sessionHasNewContent` returns false.

You set `CheckpointTranscriptStart = 0` as a workaround, which makes the next condensation re-process the **entire transcript** — inflating token counts and summary scope.

The three approaches from the design doc:

| | A: Reset cursor (current) | B: `HasCarryForward` bool | C: Infer from fields |
|---|---|---|---|
| Token counting | Inflated (full transcript) | Correct (delta only) | Correct (delta only) |
| Summary scope | Full transcript | Delta only | Delta only |
| Explicitness | Implicit | Explicit | Implicit |

### The fundamental tension

With one-checkpoint-per-commit, after carry-forward the next commit's checkpoint will have **zero new transcript content** (agent hasn't said anything new between the two commits). The checkpoint essentially says "these files were touched" but has no meaningful transcript delta or token usage for that specific commit — because the agent did all the work before commit 1.

So the question is: what should a carry-forward checkpoint contain?

- **With approach A**: Full transcript again (duplicate, inflated, but "complete")
- **With approach B/C**: Empty transcript delta (accurate but the checkpoint is basically just file metadata)

You're right on both counts. The transcript *will* have new lines after commit 1 — the agent's `git add`, `git commit` tool calls, etc. So `sessionHasNewContent` would likely return true naturally without any workaround.

But you've identified the deeper problem: that transcript content is **mechanically accurate but semantically wrong**. The second checkpoint would say:

```
Transcript: "I ran git add C.txt && git commit -m 'add C'"
Files touched: [C.txt]
```

But the actual intellectual work that produced C.txt — the reasoning, the code generation, the tool calls to write the file — all happened before commit 1 and is captured in commit 1's checkpoint. Commit 2's checkpoint is just the bookkeeping of committing it.

So the real tension is:

**Shared checkpoint (current)**: All commits point to one transcript that accurately describes all the work. Semantically correct about *what led to the changes*, but the 1:N commit-to-checkpoint mapping is messy.

**One-per-commit (carry-forward)**: Clean 1:1 mapping, but commit 2's checkpoint transcript doesn't explain why C.txt was changed — it only explains that it was committed. The causal link between work and code change is broken for the carry-forward commits.

Neither approach gives you both a clean 1:1 mapping AND accurate per-commit transcripts — because the agent doesn't work in commit-sized chunks. It works, then the human (or agent) decides how to split the changes into commits after the fact.

**The isolation problem**: Someone looking at commit A2 in `git blame`, a PR, or `git log --format` sees `Entire-Checkpoint: abc123` and looks up that checkpoint. They see 15K tokens, 5 files touched, a long transcript. They think "wow, this one commit cost 15K tokens and all this work." But actually it was 1/3 of the picture. There's nothing on the commit itself that says "I'm part of a group of 3."

a1b2c3 (Dev A) Add auth middleware     Entire-Checkpoint: abc123
d4e5f6 (Dev B) Fix typo in README

- Commit 2 → checkpoint `bbb`: 15K tokens, full transcript  
- Commit 3 → checkpoint `ccc`: 15K tokens, full transcript

And with 1:1 and accurate deltas (approach B/C):

- Commit 1 → checkpoint `aaa`: 15K tokens, full transcript
- Commit 2 → checkpoint `bbb`: ~100 tokens, transcript says "committed file C"
- Commit 3 → checkpoint `ccc`: ~100 tokens, transcript says "committed file D"

Now commits 2 and 3 look like the agent barely did anything — but the files clearly changed substantially. "How did this file get written with 100 tokens of work?"

So the core issue is that **the unit of work (agent turn) and the unit of version control (commit) are fundamentally different things**, and any mapping between them will be lossy. You either:

- Duplicate and inflate (1:1 with full data)
- Leave gaps (1:1 with accurate deltas)
- Share and confuse (N:1 current approach)

This feels like it might need a different data model — maybe the checkpoint represents the *turn*, and commits *reference* the turn rather than *owning* it. Like a many-to-one relationship that's explicit rather than accidental.

What's your instinct on this?

The current approach is a many-to-one relationship, the issue is just that the data storage isn't good in resolving that. Like we only have a strong link from commit to a single checkpoint (through the id) but we can't know on the checkpoint if there are multiple commits involved without expensive querying. And if a checkpoint consists of multiple commits the risk gets also bigger that one of those commits is reverted / removed in a rebase or only one is cherry-picked and then it's even worse.

That's the strongest argument yet for 1:1. The data model problems with many-to-one:

**One-directional link**: Commit → checkpoint is cheap (read trailer). Checkpoint → commits requires scanning git history. There's no index.

**Partial group operations break everything**:
- Cherry-pick commit 2 to `hotfix` branch: it carries `Entire-Checkpoint: abc123`, but that checkpoint's transcript and files include work from commits 1 and 3 that don't exist on `hotfix`. The checkpoint is now lying about what happened on that branch.
- Revert commit 1: checkpoint `abc123` still describes work in commit 1 as if it happened. Commits 2 and 3 still reference it. Is the checkpoint "partially valid"?
- Interactive rebase squashes commits 1+2: now one commit has `abc123` twice? Or one gets dropped? The group relationship silently degrades.

With 1:1, each checkpoint is **self-contained**. Cherry-pick a commit and its checkpoint travels with it, describing (imperfectly) that commit's work. Revert a commit and its checkpoint becomes naturally orphaned. Rebase and squash — each resulting commit still has its own checkpoint. No hidden group dependencies that silently break.

The transcript gap on carry-forward commits is a known, bounded imperfection. The many-to-one integrity issues are unbounded — they compound with every git operation and are invisible until someone inspects the data.

So: 1:1 is the more resilient model. The question becomes how to make the carry-forward checkpoints as useful as possible despite the transcript limitation. Want to think through what a carry-forward checkpoint should actually contain?

# Checkpoint-to-Commit Mapping: Approach Comparison

## Shared Checkpoint (current: N commits → 1 checkpoint)

### Strengths (from the checkpoint's perspective)

- Token counts are accurate on the checkpoint itself (counted once, for the real work)
- Transcript is complete and semantically correct (describes all the work that led to all the changes)

### Weaknesses (from the commit's perspective)

- Single-commit view is misleading: each commit appears to have consumed all the tokens and all the work of the full checkpoint, with no indication that other commits share it
- One-directional link: commit→checkpoint is cheap, but checkpoint→commits requires scanning git history (no index)
- Interleaved git log: same checkpoint ID scattered among unrelated commits after merge, making the grouping invisible
- Cherry-pick: checkpoint travels with one commit but describes work from sibling commits that don't exist on the target branch
- Revert: checkpoint still describes reverted work; remaining commits still reference it as if nothing changed
- Rebase/squash: group relationship silently degrades with no way to detect or repair
- No way to know from the checkpoint how many commits reference it without expensive queries

## One Checkpoint Per Commit: Checkpoint-Level Carry-Forward

Each commit gets its own unique checkpoint ID. After condensation, remaining uncommitted files are carried forward to a new minimal checkpoint. The carry-forward checkpoint contains only what's new since the last condensation.

### Example

Agent turn produces files A, B, C. User commits A+B, then C separately.

- Commit 1 → checkpoint `aaa`: 15K tokens, full transcript of the turn, files A+B
- Commit 2 → checkpoint `bbb`: ~100 tokens (just the commit actions), file C

### Strengths (from the commit's perspective)

- Self-contained: each commit owns exactly one checkpoint, no hidden shared state
- Resilient to git operations (cherry-pick, revert, rebase all work naturally)
- Clean bidirectional link: commit→checkpoint and checkpoint→commit are both simple lookups
- Token counts are accurate per-checkpoint (no duplication)

### Weaknesses (from the checkpoint's perspective)

- Carry-forward checkpoints are thin: they describe the act of committing, not the intellectual work that produced the changes
- "How was this file written with 100 tokens?" — the causal link between agent reasoning and code changes is missing for carry-forward commits
- Aggregated view across all checkpoints in a turn is accurate, but requires knowing which checkpoints belong together

## One Checkpoint Per Commit: Prompt-Level Carry-Forward

Each commit gets its own unique checkpoint ID. After condensation, remaining uncommitted files are carried forward with the **full prompt/turn context** — the complete transcript and token usage from the originating turn. Each checkpoint is a self-contained record of "what prompt produced this change."

### Example

Agent turn produces files A, B, C. User commits A+B, then C separately.

- Commit 1 → checkpoint `aaa`: 15K tokens, full transcript of the turn, files A+B
- Commit 2 → checkpoint `bbb`: 15K tokens, same full transcript, file C

Both checkpoints carry the complete reasoning that led to the changes.

### Strengths (from the commit's perspective)

- Self-contained: each commit owns exactly one checkpoint, no hidden shared state
- Resilient to git operations (cherry-pick, revert, rebase all work naturally)
- Clean bidirectional link
- Cherry-pick a commit and you get the full context of WHY the changes were made
- The transcript accurately explains the code changes, even for carry-forward commits

### Weaknesses (from the checkpoint's perspective)

- Token counts are duplicated: aggregating across checkpoints inflates totals (looks like 30K tokens were spent instead of 15K)
- Storage duplication: same transcript stored N times on the checkpoints branch
- Without a "these checkpoints share a prompt/turn" indicator, there's no way to deduplicate when aggregating

### Possible mitigation

A shared `turn_id` or `parent_checkpoint_id` field on the checkpoint metadata could link carry-forward checkpoints back to their originating turn, enabling:
- Accurate aggregation (deduplicate by turn)
- "Show me all commits from this turn" queries
- Clear indication that a checkpoint is a carry-forward vs. an original

## Shared Fundamental Issue

The unit of work (agent turn) ≠ the unit of version control (commit). Any mapping is lossy — the question is which kind of loss is more acceptable and recoverable.

Now I can see the full picture from the Jan 29 baseline. Here's how it worked:

---

**IDLE split-commit flow (Jan 29 code):**

**Commit 1** (has new content):
1. **PrepareCommitMsg**: `sessionsWithContent` is non-empty → `hasNewContent = true` → generates fresh checkpoint ID → adds trailer
2. **PostCommit**: `filterSessionsWithNewContent` returns the session → condenses → updates state:
   - `BaseCommit = newHead`
   - `CheckpointCount = 0`
   - `CondensedTranscriptLines = result.TotalTranscriptLines` (cursor moved to end of transcript)
   - `FilesTouched = nil` (cleared by condensation)
   - `LastCheckpointID = checkpointID` (saved for reuse)

**Commit 2** (no new content — transcript hasn't grown):
1. **PrepareCommitMsg**: `sessionsWithContent` is empty → falls into reuse path → checks `LastCheckpointID` is set AND `FilesTouched` is empty (post-condensation) → **reuses same checkpoint ID** → adds trailer
2. **PostCommit**: `filterSessionsWithNewContent` returns empty → no condensation → just updates `BaseCommit = newHead` for all sessions

So on Jan 29, the split-commit path was:
- **Same checkpoint ID reused** — no new condensation for commit 2
- **`CondensedTranscriptLines`** was the key: set to `result.TotalTranscriptLines` after commit 1's condensation, so `sessionHasNewContent` returns false for commit 2 (transcript hasn't grown past the cursor)
- **No token/transcript duplication** — commit 2 just reuses the ID with zero additional work
- But this means commit 2 **has no checkpoint data of its own** — it's purely referencing commit 1's checkpoint

This is the shared checkpoint (N:1) approach. There was no carry-forward or per-commit checkpoint logic at all — the `CondensedTranscriptLines` cursor explicitly prevented double-condensation, and `LastCheckpointID` reuse was the intended mechanism for subsequent commits.

- **UserPromptSubmit**: Clears `LastCheckpointID` when a new prompt starts (fresh work = fresh checkpoint)

Any cross-checkpoint reference reintroduces the fragility of shared state. The only truly resilient model is fully self-contained checkpoints with **no references to other checkpoints at all**.

Which means for prompt-level carry-forward, the choice is:

1. **Fully self-contained** (no `turn_id`/`parent_checkpoint_id`): Each checkpoint has the full transcript and tokens. Resilient to all git operations. But you can never deduplicate — aggregation always inflates. You just accept that.

2. **With cross-references** (add `turn_id`): Enables deduplication when all commits are present, but degrades when they're not. Same class of problem as shared checkpoints, just less severe (the data is duplicated, so nothing is *lost* — the reference is just stale).

Option 2 is at least **gracefully degrading** — a broken `turn_id` reference doesn't lose data, it just means you can't deduplicate. Whereas with shared checkpoints, a cherry-pick means you reference data that includes work from commits that don't exist on your branch.

# Checkpoint-to-Commit Mapping: Approach Comparison

## Context

The unit of work (agent turn) ≠ the unit of version control (commit). When an agent turn produces files A, B, C and the user splits them across multiple commits, we need a strategy for linking commits to checkpoint data.

We also considered a "checkpoint-level carry-forward" approach where carry-forward checkpoints only contain the delta since the last condensation (minimal transcript, near-zero tokens). This combines the weaknesses of both approaches: thin checkpoints that don't explain the changes (like 1:1) while still needing cross-references to be useful (like 1:N). It is not considered further.

## Shared Checkpoint (1:N — current implementation)

Multiple commits reference the same checkpoint ID. Condensation happens once per turn. Subsequent commits reuse `LastCheckpointID`.

### Example

Agent turn produces files A, B, C. User commits A+B, then C.

- Commit 1 → `Entire-Checkpoint: aaa` (15K tokens, full transcript)
- Commit 2 → `Entire-Checkpoint: aaa` (same checkpoint, no new condensation)

### Strengths (from the checkpoint's perspective)

- Token counts are accurate (counted once, for the real work done)
- Transcript is complete and semantically correct (describes all the work that led to all the changes)

### Weaknesses (from the commit's perspective)

- Single-commit view is misleading: each commit appears to have consumed all the tokens and all the work of the full checkpoint, with no indication that other commits share it
- One-directional link: commit→checkpoint is cheap, but checkpoint→commits requires scanning git history (no index)
- Interleaved git log: same checkpoint ID scattered among unrelated commits after merge, making the grouping invisible
- Cherry-pick: checkpoint travels with one commit but describes work from sibling commits that don't exist on the target branch
- Revert: checkpoint still describes reverted work; remaining commits still reference it as if nothing changed
- Rebase/squash: group relationship silently degrades with no way to detect or repair

## One Checkpoint Per Commit with Prompt-Level Carry-Forward (1:1)

Each commit gets its own unique checkpoint ID. After condensation, remaining uncommitted files are carried forward with the full prompt/turn context — complete transcript and token usage. Each checkpoint is a self-contained record of "what prompt produced this change."

### Example

Agent turn produces files A, B, C. User commits A+B, then C.

- Commit 1 → `Entire-Checkpoint: aaa` (15K tokens, full transcript, files A+B)
- Commit 2 → `Entire-Checkpoint: bbb` (~15.1K tokens, full transcript + small addition from commit actions, file C)

### Strengths (from the commit's perspective)

- Self-contained: each commit owns exactly one checkpoint, no hidden shared state
- Resilient to git operations (cherry-pick, revert, rebase all work naturally — no group dependencies to break)
- Clean bidirectional link: commit→checkpoint and checkpoint→commit are both simple lookups
- Cherry-pick a commit and you get the full context of why the changes were made

### Weaknesses (from the checkpoint's perspective)

- Token counts are nearly duplicated: aggregating across checkpoints inflates totals (~30.1K reported vs 15.1K actual)
- Storage duplication: same transcript stored N times on the checkpoints branch
- Individual checkpoints don't indicate they share a turn with other checkpoints

### Mitigation

The session ID (already present on every checkpoint) is the natural grouping key. All checkpoints from the same turn share the same session ID, enabling future aggregation and deduplication without adding cross-references to the checkpoint data model.

A turn ID is actually more useful than a counter here. It's just a unique ID generated at turn start (`EventTurnStart`), stored on every checkpoint created during that turn. More granular than session ID (which spans many turns), but no cross-references needed.

The limitation you're hitting with the counter — not knowing on commit 1 that commit 2 is coming — is fundamental. You can't signal "I'm part of a group" at creation time because you don't know the group size yet.

But I'd argue that's fine. The turn ID doesn't need to signal "there are siblings." It just needs to let you **discover** them when you care:

```
turn_id: turn_xyz  →  query checkpoints branch  →  found 3 checkpoints with turn_xyz
```

Most of the time (single commit per turn) it's redundant. In the multi-commit case, it's a lookup key that's cheaper than scanning by session ID + timestamp range.

It's a lightweight addition — one field in checkpoint metadata, set once at turn start, no updates needed. Costs almost nothing now, gives you a precise correlation key later if you ever build that data model. And unlike cross-references, it can't break — it's just a value, not a pointer.

From the code at HEAD, the reuse logic lives in `PrepareCommitMsg`. Here's the flow:

**Step 1**: Check if any session has new content (`filterSessionsWithNewContent` → calls `sessionHasNewContent` which checks if transcript lines > `CheckpointTranscriptStart`).

**Step 2a — New content exists**: Generate a new checkpoint ID. Or if `PendingCheckpointID` is set (from a prior mid-turn commit in the `ACTIVE_COMMITTED` deferred flow), reuse that.

**Step 2b — No new content**: Enter the reuse path:

1. Get current HEAD hash
2. Filter sessions to only those where `BaseCommit == currentHead` (prevents reusing IDs from stale sessions)
3. Get the list of staged files (`getStagedFiles`)
4. For each matching session, check:
   - `LastCheckpointID` is non-empty, AND
   - Either `FilesTouched` is empty (post-condensation, all files already committed) OR staged files overlap with `FilesTouched`
5. If a match is found → reuse that session's `LastCheckpointID`
6. If no match → no trailer added (unrelated commit)

There's also a fallback added later: if `FilesTouched` is empty AND `StepCount == 0` (both cleared by condensation), it calls `getCondensedFilesTouched` to read the file list from the already-condensed checkpoint metadata on `entire/checkpoints/v1`. This lets the overlap check work even after condensation cleared `FilesTouched`.

**When `LastCheckpointID` gets set**: In `condenseAndUpdateState`, after successful condensation: `state.LastCheckpointID = checkpointID`.

**When `LastCheckpointID` gets cleared**: In `InitializeSession` (user-prompt-submit hook), when a new prompt starts: `state.LastCheckpointID = ""`.

So the reuse window is: after condensation, until the user enters a new prompt. Any commits in that window with overlapping files get the same checkpoint ID.

# 1:1 Checkpoint-to-Commit with Prompt-Level Carry-Forward

## Context

Currently, multiple commits can share the same checkpoint ID (1:N mapping). This causes problems: misleading single-commit views, broken references after cherry-pick/revert/rebase, and no way to discover sibling commits from a checkpoint. See `checkpoint-approaches.md` for the full comparison.

We're switching to 1:1: every commit gets its own unique checkpoint. When a turn's work is split across multiple commits, each carry-forward checkpoint contains the **full prompt/turn context** (complete transcript, token usage) — not just a thin delta. This duplicates storage but makes each checkpoint self-contained and resilient to git operations.

## Starting Point

Discard all working tree changes (`git checkout -- .`) and implement fresh from HEAD.

## Implementation Steps

### Step 1: Remove `ACTIVE_COMMITTED` phase

**`cmd/entire/cli/session/phase.go`**:
- Remove `PhaseActiveCommitted` constant (line 16)
- Remove from `allPhases` (line 20)
- Remove from `PhaseFromString` — keep as backward compat mapping to `PhaseIdle` (existing sessions with this phase should degrade gracefully)
- Remove `p == PhaseActiveCommitted` from `IsActive()` (line 44)
- Remove `ActionMigrateShadowBranch` from `Action` const block (line 99)
- Remove `transitionFromActiveCommitted` function entirely
- Remove `ActionMigrateShadowBranch` case from `Transition` switch
- Remove from `ApplyCommonActions` passthrough list
- Remove from `MermaidDiagram` generation
- Update `transitionFromActive`: `EventGitCommit` → `PhaseActive + ActionCondense` (instead of `PhaseActiveCommitted + ActionMigrateShadowBranch`)

**`cmd/entire/cli/session/phase_test.go`**:
- Update `TestPhaseFromString`: `active_committed` should map to `PhaseIdle` (backward compat)
- Update `TestPhase_IsActive`: remove `ACTIVE_COMMITTED` assertion
- Update `TestTransitionFromActive`: `EventGitCommit` → `PhaseActive + ActionCondense`
- Remove any `ACTIVE_COMMITTED`-specific transition tests
- Update `TestMermaidDiagram` assertions

### Step 2: Remove `PendingCheckpointID` and deferred condensation

**`cmd/entire/cli/session/state.go`**:
- Remove `PendingCheckpointID` field from `State` struct (line 64)

**`cmd/entire/cli/strategy/manual_commit_hooks.go`**:
- **PostCommit**: Remove two-pass architecture, remove `pendingMigrations` slice, remove `ActionMigrateShadowBranch` case. Single pass only.
- **PrepareCommitMsg**: Remove `PendingCheckpointID` checks in new content path (lines ~362-376). Always generate fresh ID.
- **`addTrailerForAgentCommit`**: Remove `PendingCheckpointID` usage, always `id.Generate()`
- **`handleAmendCommitMsg`**: Remove `PendingCheckpointID` restoration path, keep only `LastCheckpointID` for trailer restoration on amend
- **`condenseAndUpdateState`**: Remove `state.PendingCheckpointID = ""` line
- **`HandleTurnEnd`**: Remove `ActionCondense` dispatching — no deferred condensation. Keep the method but it becomes a no-op for strategy actions.
- **`handleTurnEndCondense`**: Remove entire method
- **`InitializeSession`**: Remove `PendingCheckpointID` clearing

**`cmd/entire/cli/strategy/manual_commit_migration.go`**:
- Remove `migrateShadowBranchIfNeeded` method
- Remove `migrateAndPersistIfNeeded` method (check if SaveChanges/SaveTaskCheckpoint call this — if so, update those callers)

### Step 3: Remove `LastCheckpointID` reuse path in PrepareCommitMsg

**`cmd/entire/cli/strategy/manual_commit_hooks.go`**:
- Remove the entire "no new content" reuse block in PrepareCommitMsg (the block that checks `LastCheckpointID`, `getCondensedFilesTouched`, and `hasOverlappingFiles`)
- Remove `getCondensedFilesTouched` method
- Remove `reusedSession` variable and its usage
- Simplify: if no new content and no carry-forward → no trailer added
- **Keep `LastCheckpointID`** — it's still needed for amend trailer restoration (`handleAmendCommitMsg`)

**`cmd/entire/cli/strategy/manual_commit_session.go`**:
- Update cleanup logic that references `LastCheckpointID` (lines ~85, 91)

### Step 4: Immediate condensation for ACTIVE sessions

**`cmd/entire/cli/strategy/manual_commit_hooks.go`** — PostCommit:
- `ACTIVE + GitCommit` now produces `ActionCondense` (from Step 1)
- Handle it same as IDLE condensation: call `condenseAndUpdateState` when `hasNew`
- Track `condensed` bool per session
- Track `uncondensedActiveOnBranch` (only uncondensed active sessions prevent shadow branch deletion)

### Step 5: Add carry-forward logic

**`cmd/entire/cli/strategy/manual_commit_hooks.go`**:

Add helper `filesChangedInCommit(commit *object.Commit) map[string]struct{}`:
- Diff commit vs parent tree, return set of changed file paths
- Pattern from `explain.go:1543-1563`

Add helper `subtractFiles(files []string, exclude map[string]struct{}) []string`:
- Set subtraction

Add method `carryForwardToNewShadowBranch(logCtx, repo, state, remainingFiles)`:
- Call `store.WriteTemporary()` with remaining files at new HEAD (`state.BaseCommit`, already updated by condensation)
- Set `state.FilesTouched = remainingFiles`
- Set `state.StepCount = 1`
- Set `state.CheckpointTranscriptStart = 0` — **intentional for prompt-level carry-forward**: next condensation re-processes full transcript so the carry-forward checkpoint is self-contained
- Set `state.LastCheckpointID = ""` — next commit must generate fresh ID

In PostCommit loop, after condensation succeeds for an ACTIVE session:
```
if condensed && state.Phase.IsActive() {
    remaining := subtractFiles(filesTouchedBefore, committedFileSet)
    if len(remaining) > 0 {
        carryForwardToNewShadowBranch(...)
    }
}
```

Save `filesTouchedBefore` BEFORE action dispatch (condensation clears `FilesTouched`).
Compute `committedFileSet` once before the session loop.

# 1:1 Checkpoint-to-Commit with Prompt-Level Carry-Forward

## Context

Currently, multiple commits can share the same checkpoint ID (1:N mapping). This causes problems: misleading single-commit views, broken references after cherry-pick/revert/rebase, and no way to discover sibling commits from a checkpoint. See `checkpoint-approaches.md` for the full comparison.

We're switching to 1:1: every commit gets its own unique checkpoint. When a turn's work is split across multiple commits, each carry-forward checkpoint contains the **full prompt/turn context** (complete transcript, token usage) — not just a thin delta. This duplicates storage but makes each checkpoint self-contained and resilient to git operations.

A `TurnID` field is added to checkpoint metadata so related checkpoints can be discovered by querying the same turn, enabling future aggregation/deduplication.

## Starting Point

Discard all working tree changes (`git checkout -- .`) and implement fresh from HEAD.

## Implementation Steps

### Step 1: Remove `ACTIVE_COMMITTED` phase and `ActionMigrateShadowBranch`

**`cmd/entire/cli/session/phase.go`**:
- Remove `PhaseActiveCommitted` constant
- Remove from `allPhases`
- In `PhaseFromString`: map `"active_committed"` → `PhaseIdle` (backward compat for existing state files)
- Remove `p == PhaseActiveCommitted` from `IsActive()`
- Remove `ActionMigrateShadowBranch` from Action const block and `String()`
- Remove `transitionFromActiveCommitted` function entirely
- Remove its case from `Transition` switch
- Remove from `ApplyCommonActions` passthrough list
- Update `transitionFromActive`: `EventGitCommit` → `PhaseActive + [ActionCondense, ActionUpdateLastInteraction]`

**`cmd/entire/cli/session/phase_test.go`**:
- `TestPhaseFromString`: `"active_committed"` maps to `PhaseIdle`
- `TestPhase_IsActive`: only ACTIVE returns true
- `TestTransitionFromActive`: GitCommit → ACTIVE + ActionCondense
- Remove ACTIVE_COMMITTED transition tests
- Update backward compat test
- Update Mermaid diagram assertions

### Step 2: Remove `PendingCheckpointID` and deferred condensation

**`cmd/entire/cli/session/state.go`**:
- Remove `PendingCheckpointID` field

**`cmd/entire/cli/strategy/manual_commit_hooks.go`**:
- **PostCommit**: Remove two-pass architecture, `pendingMigrations`, `ActionMigrateShadowBranch` case. Single pass.
- **PrepareCommitMsg**: Remove `PendingCheckpointID` checks in new content path. Always `id.Generate()`.
- **`addTrailerForAgentCommit`**: Always `id.Generate()`
- **`handleAmendCommitMsg`**: Remove `PendingCheckpointID` restoration, keep `LastCheckpointID` only
- **`condenseAndUpdateState`**: Remove `state.PendingCheckpointID = ""` line
- **`HandleTurnEnd`**: Remove `ActionCondense` dispatching (no deferred condensation)
- **`handleTurnEndCondense`**: Delete entire method
- **`InitializeSession`**: Remove `PendingCheckpointID` clearing

**`cmd/entire/cli/strategy/manual_commit_migration.go`**:
- Remove `migrateShadowBranchIfNeeded` and `migrateAndPersistIfNeeded` (update callers in SaveChanges/SaveTaskCheckpoint if needed)

### Step 3: Remove `LastCheckpointID` reuse path in PrepareCommitMsg

**`cmd/entire/cli/strategy/manual_commit_hooks.go`**:
- Remove the entire "no new content" block that checks `LastCheckpointID`, calls `getCondensedFilesTouched`, `hasOverlappingFiles`
- Delete `getCondensedFilesTouched` method
- Remove `reusedSession` variable
- Simplify: no new content and no carry-forward → no trailer
- **Keep `LastCheckpointID` field** — still needed for amend trailer restoration in `handleAmendCommitMsg`

### Step 4: Immediate condensation + carry-forward in PostCommit

**`cmd/entire/cli/strategy/manual_commit_hooks.go`**:

Add helpers:
- `filesChangedInCommit(commit) map[string]struct{}` — diff commit vs parent (pattern from `explain.go:1543-1563`)
- `subtractFiles(files []string, exclude map[string]struct{}) []string`

Add `carryForwardToNewShadowBranch(logCtx, repo, state, remainingFiles)`:
- `store.WriteTemporary()` with remaining files at `state.BaseCommit` (new HEAD)
- `state.FilesTouched = remainingFiles`
- `state.StepCount = 1`
- `state.CheckpointTranscriptStart = 0` — **intentional**: prompt-level carry-forward means next condensation re-processes full transcript
- `state.LastCheckpointID = ""` — next commit generates fresh ID

PostCommit loop changes:
- Compute `committedFileSet` once before session loop
- Save `filesTouchedBefore` before action dispatch (condensation clears `FilesTouched`)
- Track `condensed` bool per session
- After condensation for ACTIVE sessions: `subtractFiles(filesTouchedBefore, committedFileSet)` → carry forward if remaining
- Track `uncondensedActiveOnBranch` instead of `activeSessionsOnBranch`

### Step 5: Add `TurnID`

**`cmd/entire/cli/session/state.go`**:
- Add `TurnID string `json:"turn_id,omitempty"``

**`cmd/entire/cli/strategy/manual_commit_hooks.go`** — `InitializeSession`:
- Generate `TurnID` via `id.Generate()` on every turn start

**`cmd/entire/cli/checkpoint/checkpoint.go`** — `CommittedMetadata`:
- Add `TurnID string `json:"turn_id,omitempty"``

**`cmd/entire/cli/checkpoint/committed.go`** — `WriteCommitted` / `WriteCommittedOptions`:
- Add `TurnID` field, wire through to `CommittedMetadata`

**`cmd/entire/cli/strategy/manual_commit_condensation.go`** — `CondenseSession`:
- Pass `state.TurnID` through to `WriteCommitted`

### Step 6: Update tests

**Unit tests**:
- `phase_postcommit_test.go`: Update existing, add carry-forward tests (partial commit + all-committed)
- `phase_prepare_commit_msg_test.go`: Remove `PendingCheckpointID` refs, verify fresh IDs
- `phase_wiring_test.go`: Add `TurnID` assertion in `InitializeSession` tests
- `mid_turn_commit_test.go`: Update if referencing removed concepts

**Integration tests**:
- `last_checkpoint_id_test.go`: Remove `ReusedAcrossCommits` test, rewrite `BaseCommitUpdatedOnReuse` as carry-forward test. Keep amend-related tests.
- `phase_transitions_test.go`: Verify immediate condensation in `CommitBeforeStop`

### Step 7: Clean up references

- `cmd/entire/cli/doctor.go`: Remove `ACTIVE_COMMITTED` refs
- `cmd/entire/cli/hooks.go` / `hooks_claudecode_handlers.go`: Verify `HandleTurnEnd` works with no strategy actions
- `cmd/entire/cli/reset.go`: Remove `ACTIVE_COMMITTED` refs
- `cmd/entire/cli/strategy/strategy.go`: Remove `PendingCheckpointID` refs

## Files to Modify

| File | Change |
|------|--------|
| `session/phase.go` | Remove ACTIVE_COMMITTED, ActionMigrateShadowBranch; ACTIVE+GitCommit → ActionCondense |
| `session/state.go` | Remove PendingCheckpointID; add TurnID |
| `session/phase_test.go` | Update transitions |
| `strategy/manual_commit_hooks.go` | Single-pass PostCommit, carry-forward, remove reuse path, remove deferred condensation |
| `strategy/manual_commit_migration.go` | Remove migration methods |
| `strategy/manual_commit_condensation.go` | Wire TurnID |
| `checkpoint/checkpoint.go` | Add TurnID to CommittedMetadata |
| `checkpoint/committed.go` | Wire TurnID through WriteCommitted |
| `strategy/phase_postcommit_test.go` | Update + add carry-forward tests |
| `strategy/phase_prepare_commit_msg_test.go` | Update amend tests |
| `strategy/phase_wiring_test.go` | TurnID assertions |
| `integration_test/last_checkpoint_id_test.go` | Remove reuse test, add carry-forward |
| `integration_test/phase_transitions_test.go` | Update assertions |
| `cli/doctor.go`, `cli/hooks.go`, `cli/reset.go` | Remove ACTIVE_COMMITTED refs |

## Verification

```bash
mise run fmt && mise run lint && mise run test:ci
```

Summary:
1. Primary Request and Intent:
   The user wanted to redesign the checkpoint-to-commit mapping from a shared checkpoint model (N commits → 1 checkpoint) to a 1:1 model where every commit gets its own unique checkpoint. Through extensive discussion, the user and I explored three approaches:
   - **Shared checkpoint (current)**: Multiple commits share one checkpoint ID. Accurate token counts but misleading per-commit views, fragile under git operations (cherry-pick, revert, rebase).
   - **Checkpoint-level carry-forward**: Each commit gets own ID but carry-forward checkpoints are thin (minimal transcript). Rejected as "worst of both worlds."
   - **Prompt-level carry-forward (chosen)**: Each commit gets own ID with full prompt/turn context duplicated. Self-contained, resilient to git operations. Accepts storage duplication.
   
   Additionally, a `TurnID` field should be added to checkpoint metadata for future correlation of related checkpoints within a turn.

2. Key Technical Concepts:
   - **Session state machine**: Phases (IDLE, ACTIVE, ENDED — ACTIVE_COMMITTED being removed), Events (TurnStart, TurnEnd, GitCommit), Actions (ActionCondense, etc.)

   449→// InitialAttribution captures line-level attribution metrics at commit time.
   450→// This is a point-in-time snapshot comparing the checkpoint tree (agent work)
   451→// against the committed tree (may include human edits).
   452→//
   453→// Attribution Metrics:
   454→//   - TotalCommitted measures "net additions" (lines added that remain in the commit)
   455→//   - AgentPercentage represents "of the new code added, what percentage came from the agent"
   456→//   - Deletion work is tracked separately in HumanRemoved (not included in percentage)
   457→//
   458→// Deletion-Only Commits:
   459→// For commits with only deletions (no additions), TotalCommitted will be 0 and
   460→// AgentPercentage will be 0. This is by design - the percentage metric is only
   461→// meaningful for commits that add code. Deletion contributions are captured in
   462→// the HumanRemoved field but don't affect the attribution percentage.
   463→type InitialAttribution struct {
   464→	CalculatedAt    time.Time `json:"calculated_at"`
   465→	AgentLines      int       `json:"agent_lines"`      // Lines added by agent (base → shadow diff)
   466→	HumanAdded      int       `json:"human_added"`      // Lines added by human (excluding modifications)
   467→	HumanModified   int       `json:"human_modified"`   // Lines modified by human (estimate: min(added, removed))
   468→	HumanRemoved    int       `json:"human_removed"`    // Lines removed by human (excluding modifications)
   469→	TotalCommitted  int       `json:"total_committed"`  // Net additions in commit (agent + human new lines, not total file size)
   470→	AgentPercentage float64   `json:"agent_percentage"` // agent_lines / total_committed * 100 (0 for deletion-only commits)
   471→}

    30→// listCheckpoints returns all checkpoints from the metadata branch.
    31→// Uses checkpoint.GitStore.ListCommitted() for reading from entire/checkpoints/v1.
    32→func (s *ManualCommitStrategy) listCheckpoints() ([]CheckpointInfo, error) {
    33→	store, err := s.getCheckpointStore()
    34→	if err != nil {
    35→		return nil, fmt.Errorf("failed to get checkpoint store: %w", err)
    36→	}
    37→
    38→	committed, err := store.ListCommitted(context.Background())
    39→	if err != nil {
    40→		return nil, fmt.Errorf("failed to list committed checkpoints: %w", err)
    41→	}
    42→
    43→	// Convert from checkpoint.CommittedInfo to strategy.CheckpointInfo
    44→	result := make([]CheckpointInfo, 0, len(committed))
    45→	for _, c := range committed {
    46→		result = append(result, CheckpointInfo{
    47→			CheckpointID:     c.CheckpointID,
    48→			SessionID:        c.SessionID,
    49→			CreatedAt:        c.CreatedAt,
    50→			CheckpointsCount: c.CheckpointsCount,
    51→			FilesTouched:     c.FilesTouched,
    52→			Agent:            c.Agent,
    53→			IsTask:           c.IsTask,
    54→			ToolUseID:        c.ToolUseID,
    55→			SessionCount:     c.SessionCount,
    56→			SessionIDs:       c.SessionIDs,
    57→		})
    58→	}
    59→
    60→	return result, nil
    61→}

    63→// getCheckpointsForSession returns all checkpoints for a session ID.
    64→func (s *ManualCommitStrategy) getCheckpointsForSession(sessionID string) ([]CheckpointInfo, error) {
    65→	all, err := s.listCheckpoints()
    66→	if err != nil {
    67→		return nil, err
    68→	}
    69→
    70→	var result []CheckpointInfo
    71→	for _, cp := range all {
    72→		if cp.SessionID == sessionID || strings.HasPrefix(cp.SessionID, sessionID) {
    73→			result = append(result, cp)
    74→		}
    75→	}
    76→
    77→	if len(result) == 0 {
    78→		return nil, fmt.Errorf("no checkpoints for session: %s", sessionID)
    79→	}
    80→
    81→	return result, nil
    82→}

   106→// CondenseSession condenses a session's shadow branch to permanent storage.
   107→// checkpointID is the 12-hex-char value from the Entire-Checkpoint trailer.
   108→// Metadata is stored at sharded path: <checkpoint_id[:2]>/<checkpoint_id[2:]>/
   109→// Uses checkpoint.GitStore.WriteCommitted for the git operations.
   110→func (s *ManualCommitStrategy) CondenseSession(repo *git.Repository, checkpointID id.CheckpointID, state *SessionState) (*CondenseResult, error) {
   111→	// Get shadow branch
   112→	shadowBranchName := getShadowBranchNameForCommit(state.BaseCommit, state.WorktreeID)
   113→	refName := plumbing.NewBranchReferenceName(shadowBranchName)
   114→	ref, err := repo.Reference(refName, true)
   115→	if err != nil {
   116→		return nil, fmt.Errorf("shadow branch not found: %w", err)
   117→	}
   118→
   119→	// Extract session data from the shadow branch (with live transcript fallback).
   120→	// Use tracked files from session state instead of collecting all files from tree.
   121→	// Pass agent type to handle different transcript formats (JSONL for Claude, JSON for Gemini).
   122→	// Pass live transcript path so condensation reads the current file rather than a
   123→	// potentially stale shadow branch copy (SaveChanges may have been skipped if the
   124→	// last turn had no code changes).
   125→	// Pass CheckpointTranscriptStart for accurate token calculation (line offset for Claude, message index for Gemini).
   126→	sessionData, err := s.extractSessionData(repo, ref.Hash(), state.SessionID, state.FilesTouched, state.AgentType, state.TranscriptPath, state.CheckpointTranscriptStart)
   127→	if err != nil {
   128→		return nil, fmt.Errorf("failed to extract session data: %w", err)
   129→	}
   130→
   131→	// Get checkpoint store
   132→	store, err := s.getCheckpointStore()
   133→	if err != nil {
   134→		return nil, fmt.Errorf("failed to get checkpoint store: %w", err)
   135→	}
   136→
   137→	// Get author info
   138→	authorName, authorEmail := GetGitAuthorFromRepo(repo)
   139→	attribution := calculateSessionAttributions(repo, ref, sessionData, state)
   140→	// Get current branch name
   141→	branchName := GetCurrentBranchName(repo)
   142→
   143→	// Generate summary if enabled
   144→	var summary *cpkg.Summary
   145→	if settings.IsSummarizeEnabled() && len(sessionData.Transcript) > 0 {
   146→		logCtx := logging.WithComponent(context.Background(), "attribution")
   147→		summarizeCtx := logging.WithComponent(logCtx, "summarize")
   148→
   149→		// Scope transcript to this checkpoint's portion.
   150→		// SliceFromLine only works for JSONL (Claude Code) transcripts where
   151→		// CheckpointTranscriptStart is a line offset. For Gemini JSON transcripts,
   152→		// CheckpointTranscriptStart is a message index and the transcript is a single
   153→		// JSON blob, so line-based slicing would produce malformed content.
   154→		// The summarizer (ParseFromBytes) only supports JSONL, so skip scoping for Gemini.
   155→		var scopedTranscript []byte
   156→		if state.AgentType == agent.AgentTypeGemini {
   157→			scopedTranscript = sessionData.Transcript
   158→		} else {
   159→			scopedTranscript = transcript.SliceFromLine(sessionData.Transcript, state.CheckpointTranscriptStart)
   160→		}
   161→		if len(scopedTranscript) > 0 {
   162→			var err error
   163→			summary, err = summarize.GenerateFromTranscript(summarizeCtx, scopedTranscript, sessionData.FilesTouched, nil)
   164→			if err != nil {
   165→				logging.Warn(summarizeCtx, "summary generation failed",
   166→					slog.String("session_id", state.SessionID),
   167→					slog.String("error", err.Error()))
   168→				// Continue without summary - non-blocking
   169→			} else {
   170→				logging.Info(summarizeCtx, "summary generated",
   171→					slog.String("session_id", state.SessionID))
   172→			}
   173→		}
   174→	}
   175→
   176→	// Write checkpoint metadata using the checkpoint store
   177→	if err := store.WriteCommitted(context.Background(), cpkg.WriteCommittedOptions{
   178→		CheckpointID:                checkpointID,
   179→		SessionID:                   state.SessionID,
   180→		Strategy:                    StrategyNameManualCommit,
   181→		Branch:                      branchName,
   182→		Transcript:                  sessionData.Transcript,
   183→		Prompts:                     sessionData.Prompts,
   184→		Context:                     sessionData.Context,
   185→		FilesTouched:                sessionData.FilesTouched,
   186→		CheckpointsCount:            state.StepCount,
   187→		EphemeralBranch:             shadowBranchName,
   188→		AuthorName:                  authorName,
   189→		AuthorEmail:                 authorEmail,
   190→		Agent:                       state.AgentType,
   191→		TranscriptIdentifierAtStart: state.TranscriptIdentifierAtStart,
   192→		CheckpointTranscriptStart:   state.CheckpointTranscriptStart,
   193→		TokenUsage:                  sessionData.TokenUsage,
   194→		InitialAttribution:          attribution,
   195→		Summary:                     summary,
   196→		SessionTranscriptPath:       homeRelativePath(state.TranscriptPath),
   197→	}); err != nil {
   198→		return nil, fmt.Errorf("failed to write checkpoint metadata: %w", err)
   199→	}
   200→
   201→	return &CondenseResult{
   202→		CheckpointID:         checkpointID,
   203→		SessionID:            state.SessionID,
   204→		CheckpointsCount:     state.StepCount,
   205→		FilesTouched:         sessionData.FilesTouched,
   206→		TotalTranscriptLines: sessionData.FullTranscriptLines,
   207→	}, nil
   208→}

   210→func calculateSessionAttributions(repo *git.Repository, shadowRef *plumbing.Reference, sessionData *ExtractedSessionData, state *SessionState) *cpkg.InitialAttribution {
   211→	// Calculate initial attribution using accumulated prompt attribution data.
   212→	// This uses user edits captured at each prompt start (before agent works),
   213→	// plus any user edits after the final checkpoint (shadow → head).
   214→	logCtx := logging.WithComponent(context.Background(), "attribution")
   215→	var attribution *cpkg.InitialAttribution
   216→	headRef, headErr := repo.Head()
   217→	if headErr != nil {
   218→		logging.Debug(logCtx, "attribution skipped: failed to get HEAD",
   219→			slog.String("error", headErr.Error()))
   220→	} else {
   221→		headCommit, commitErr := repo.CommitObject(headRef.Hash())
   222→		if commitErr != nil {
   223→			logging.Debug(logCtx, "attribution skipped: failed to get HEAD commit",
   224→				slog.String("error", commitErr.Error()))
   225→		} else {
   226→			headTree, treeErr := headCommit.Tree()
   227→			if treeErr != nil {
   228→				logging.Debug(logCtx, "attribution skipped: failed to get HEAD tree",
   229→					slog.String("error", treeErr.Error()))
   230→			} else {
   231→				// Get shadow branch tree (checkpoint tree - what the agent wrote)
   232→				shadowCommit, shadowErr := repo.CommitObject(shadowRef.Hash())
   233→				if shadowErr != nil {
   234→					logging.Debug(logCtx, "attribution skipped: failed to get shadow commit",
   235→						slog.String("error", shadowErr.Error()),
   236→						slog.String("shadow_ref", shadowRef.Hash().String()))
   237→				} else {
   238→					shadowTree, shadowTreeErr := shadowCommit.Tree()
   239→					if shadowTreeErr != nil {
   240→						logging.Debug(logCtx, "attribution skipped: failed to get shadow tree",
   241→							slog.String("error", shadowTreeErr.Error()))
   242→					} else {
   243→						// Get base tree (state before session started)
   244→						var baseTree *object.Tree
   245→						attrBase := state.AttributionBaseCommit
   246→						if attrBase == "" {
   247→							attrBase = state.BaseCommit // backward compat
   248→						}
   249→						if baseCommit, baseErr := repo.CommitObject(plumbing.NewHash(attrBase)); baseErr == nil {
   250→							if tree, baseTErr := baseCommit.Tree(); baseTErr == nil {
   251→								baseTree = tree
   252→							} else {
   253→								logging.Debug(logCtx, "attribution: base tree unavailable",
   254→									slog.String("error", baseTErr.Error()))
   255→							}
   256→						} else {
   257→							logging.Debug(logCtx, "attribution: base commit unavailable",
   258→								slog.String("error", baseErr.Error()),
   259→								slog.String("attribution_base", attrBase))
   260→						}
   261→
   262→						// Log accumulated prompt attributions for debugging
   263→						var totalUserAdded, totalUserRemoved int
   264→						for i, pa := range state.PromptAttributions {
   265→							totalUserAdded += pa.UserLinesAdded
   266→							totalUserRemoved += pa.UserLinesRemoved
   267→							logging.Debug(logCtx, "prompt attribution data",
   268→								slog.Int("checkpoint", pa.CheckpointNumber),
   269→								slog.Int("user_added", pa.UserLinesAdded),
   270→								slog.Int("user_removed", pa.UserLinesRemoved),
   271→								slog.Int("agent_added", pa.AgentLinesAdded),
   272→								slog.Int("agent_removed", pa.AgentLinesRemoved),
   273→								slog.Int("index", i))
   274→						}
   275→
   276→						attribution = CalculateAttributionWithAccumulated(
   277→							baseTree,
   278→							shadowTree,
   279→							headTree,
   280→							sessionData.FilesTouched,
   281→							state.PromptAttributions,
   282→						)
   283→
   284→						if attribution != nil {
   285→							logging.Info(logCtx, "attribution calculated",
   286→								slog.Int("agent_lines", attribution.AgentLines),
   287→								slog.Int("human_added", attribution.HumanAdded),

   289→								slog.Int("human_removed", attribution.HumanRemoved),

   304→// extractSessionData extracts session data from the shadow branch.
   305→// filesTouched is the list of files tracked during the session (from SessionState.FilesTouched).
   306→// agentType identifies the agent (e.g., "Gemini CLI", "Claude Code") to determine transcript format.
   307→// liveTranscriptPath, when non-empty and readable, is preferred over the shadow branch copy.
   308→// This handles the case where SaveChanges was skipped (no code changes) but the transcript
   309→// continued growing — the shadow branch copy would be stale.
   310→// checkpointTranscriptStart is the line offset (Claude) or message index (Gemini) where the current checkpoint began.
   311→func (s *ManualCommitStrategy) extractSessionData(repo *git.Repository, shadowRef plumbing.Hash, sessionID string, filesTouched []string, agentType agent.AgentType, liveTranscriptPath string, checkpointTranscriptStart int) (*ExtractedSessionData, error) {
   312→	commit, err := repo.CommitObject(shadowRef)
   313→	if err != nil {
   314→		return nil, fmt.Errorf("failed to get commit object: %w", err)
   315→	}
   316→
   317→	tree, err := commit.Tree()
   318→	if err != nil {
   319→		return nil, fmt.Errorf("failed to get commit tree: %w", err)
   320→	}
   321→
   322→	data := &ExtractedSessionData{}
   323→	// sessionID is already an "entire session ID" (with date prefix)
   324→	metadataDir := paths.SessionMetadataDirFromSessionID(sessionID)
   325→
   326→	// Extract transcript — prefer the live file when available, fall back to shadow branch.
   327→	// The shadow branch copy may be stale if the last turn ended without code changes
   328→	// (SaveChanges is only called when there are file modifications).
   329→	var fullTranscript string
   330→	if liveTranscriptPath != "" {
   331→		if liveData, readErr := os.ReadFile(liveTranscriptPath); readErr == nil && len(liveData) > 0 { //nolint:gosec // path from session state
   332→			fullTranscript = string(liveData)

   334→	}
   335→	if fullTranscript == "" {
   336→		// Fall back to shadow branch copy
   337→		if file, fileErr := tree.File(metadataDir + "/" + paths.TranscriptFileName); fileErr == nil {
   338→			if content, contentErr := file.Contents(); contentErr == nil {
   339→				fullTranscript = content
   340→			}
   341→		} else if file, fileErr := tree.File(metadataDir + "/" + paths.TranscriptFileNameLegacy); fileErr == nil {
   342→			if content, contentErr := file.Contents(); contentErr == nil {
   343→				fullTranscript = content
   344→			}
   345→		}
   346→	}
   347→
   348→	// Process transcript based on agent type
   349→	if fullTranscript != "" {
   350→		data.Transcript = []byte(fullTranscript)
   351→		data.FullTranscriptLines = countTranscriptItems(agentType, fullTranscript)
   352→		data.Prompts = extractUserPrompts(agentType, fullTranscript)
   353→		data.Context = generateContextFromPrompts(data.Prompts)

   367→// countTranscriptItems counts lines (JSONL) or messages (JSON) in a transcript.
   368→// For Claude Code and JSONL-based agents, this counts lines.
   369→// For Gemini CLI and JSON-based agents, this counts messages.
   370→// Returns 0 if the content is empty or malformed.
   371→func countTranscriptItems(agentType agent.AgentType, content string) int {
   372→	if content == "" {
   373→		return 0
   374→	}
   375→
   376→	// Try Gemini format first if agentType is Gemini, or as fallback if Unknown
   377→	if agentType == agent.AgentTypeGemini || agentType == agent.AgentTypeUnknown {
   378→		transcript, err := geminicli.ParseTranscript([]byte(content))
   379→		if err == nil && transcript != nil && len(transcript.Messages) > 0 {
   380→			return len(transcript.Messages)
   381→		}
   382→		// If agentType is explicitly Gemini but parsing failed, return 0
   383→		if agentType == agent.AgentTypeGemini {
   384→			return 0
   385→		}
   386→		// Otherwise fall through to JSONL parsing for Unknown type
   387→	}
   388→
   389→	// Claude Code and other JSONL-based agents
   390→	allLines := strings.Split(content, "\n")
   391→	// Trim trailing empty lines (from final \n in JSONL)
   392→	for len(allLines) > 0 && strings.TrimSpace(allLines[len(allLines)-1]) == "" {
   393→		allLines = allLines[:len(allLines)-1]
   394→	}
   395→	return len(allLines)
   396→}
